test_title: PYST 25: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Sarkaria Commission primarily focussed on strengthening which type of federalism in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Co-operative federalism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission** was established in **1983** by the Government of India to review the center-state relations and suggest reforms for enhancing cooperation between them.
 
• The commission focused on strengthening **cooperative federalism**, which emphasizes collaboration and mutual trust between the center and the states in India.
 
• It provided recommendations for maintaining a balance of power between the central and state governments, ensuring that both could work harmoniously towards national development.
 
• One of its key recommendations was the establishment of the **Inter-State Council** under **Article 263** of the Indian Constitution, aimed at promoting dialogue and resolving disputes between the center and states.
 
• The commission also emphasized the need for consultations between the center and states before enacting laws on subjects in the concurrent list. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Co-operative federalism:**

 
 
• **Cooperative federalism** refers to a system where the center and the states work collaboratively to achieve national goals while respecting the autonomy of each level of government.
 
• It promotes shared responsibility and mutual trust between the center and states, ensuring effective governance and policy implementation.
 
• Examples include coordination in implementing national schemes like **Swachh Bharat Mission**, **Digital India**, and **GST**.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal federalism:**
 
 
• Fiscal federalism relates to financial relations between units of governments in a federal system.
 
• It involves the allocation of resources and revenue-sharing between the center and states, as guided by bodies like the **Finance Commission**.
 
• Examples include the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, which ensures a unified tax regime across the country.
 
 
 
• **Unitary federalism:**
 
 
• Unitary federalism refers to a system where the central government holds significant authority, and states have limited autonomy.
 
• India follows a quasi-federal structure, where the center has stronger powers compared to the states, especially during emergencies under **Articles 352, 356, and 360**.
 
 
 
• **Competitive federalism:**
 
 
• **Competitive federalism** promotes competition among states to attract investments and improve governance.
 
• It is a modern approach where states independently work to enhance their economic performance and attract businesses.
 
• Examples include states competing to rank higher in the **Ease of Doing Business Index** published by the Government of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Sarkaria Commission** emphasized the need for decentralization and greater autonomy for states while ensuring cooperation and unity within the federal structure.
 
• The establishment of the **Inter-State Council** has been an important step in resolving inter-state disputes and enhancing coordination between the center and states.
 
• While cooperative federalism is the ideal approach, India’s federal structure also incorporates elements of unitary federalism, especially during times of national emergencies.
